sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup
sections.what: Imports the database, the scoring constants and functions, the scoring service and test helpers, and declares the shared match, team and player values.
sections.why: Provides the shared values the scoring tests build on.
sections.watch_out: Tests share these values, so later checks depend on earlier ones.

sections.name: stats
sections.title: Sample stat lines
sections.what: Defines a function that returns sample batting and bowling stat lines for two players.
sections.why: Gives the same known inputs to each scoring run.
sections.watch_out: The expected points in later checks are built from these exact numbers.

sections.name: scoring ledger: append-only, versioned, idempotent
sections.title: Scoring ledger checks
sections.what: Checks that scoring writes one versioned record per pick and that the team total comes from those records. Checks that repeated runs add no duplicates and award experience only once. Checks a new scoring version adds new records alongside the old ones. Checks the database refuses to update or delete ledger rows. Checks invalid stat lines and unknown matches are refused without writing anything.
sections.why: Likely reason: scores must be correct, repeatable and never silently changed.
sections.watch_out: The append-only protection is in the database, so removing that rule would let records be edited without any test failing in code.

summary: Tests the scoring ledger: how match stats turn into points, how each pick gets a versioned record, and that records can be added but never changed or deleted.
purpose: Makes sure scoring is correct, repeatable, and that the history of points cannot be edited.
why: Likely reason: fantasy scores are a record people rely on, so changes must be added as new rows rather than edits.
how: Creates a match, two players and a fantasy team with a captain and vice captain. Runs scoring, checks the events and team total, repeats scoring to confirm no duplicates and no extra experience, adds a new scoring version, checks the database refuses edits and deletes, and checks invalid input is rejected.
inputs: Test match, players, a fantasy team and sample stat lines.
outputs: Scoring results, ledger rows, team totals and errors.
risks: Protection against edits lives in the database, so removing it would silently allow changes. Expected totals depend on the captain and vice captain multipliers.
debug: Check the ledger rows for the match and their version numbers. If the total is wrong, compare each player's points with the scoring rules.
